supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to a ChartMate-named updater running as ben.carter from the user profile. It began at 13:37:57 and made repeated proxy requests to update.chartmate-imaging.net through 14:08; the recorded successful requests are several minutes apart.

The observed updater path is C:\Users\ben.carter\AppData\Local\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe, whereas the inventory lists the approved updater at C:\Program Files\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe. The observed hostname is update.chartmate-imaging.net, whereas the inventory lists update.chartmate-imaging.com. These discrepancies warrant validation but do not by themselves establish maliciousness.
The updater process generated a file-creation event targeting its own executable path shortly after starting.

Some requests to the updater hostname succeeded, while others were rejected with proxy status 407 or failed with status 502. The logged successful tunnels show tens of kilobytes received, not evidence of a large upload.
WS-BCARTER-01 also made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01 that resulted in an ANONYMOUS LOGON. The records do not show what share or files, if any, were accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied coverage status reports a winsec and Sysmon collection outage for WS-LPARK-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC. This does not cover WS-BCARTER-01, but limits visibility into activity on that other workstation during the review window.
The available records show proxy tunnel metadata, not the HTTPS contents or downloaded update payload.
No binary hash, signature, or vendor validation for the observed user-profile executable is present in the supplied evidence.
claims_not_established: Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is owned or authorized by ChartMate, or is an impersonating domain.
Whether the observed cmupdate.exe is a legitimate ChartMate build, a modified copy, or malware.
Whether any update or other payload was downloaded, installed, or executed by the updater.
What data, if any, was transferred beyond the proxy metadata shown in the records.
What SMB resources were accessed on FILE-HD-01, and whether the anonymous logon reflects an attempted or successful file access.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the updater executable and verify its cryptographic hash, signature, provenance, and installation history against an authenticated ChartMate source.
Validate the ownership and legitimacy of update.chartmate-imaging.net with the software vendor and compare it with the approved update.chartmate-imaging.com domain.
Collect TLS inspection, proxy, or endpoint download records sufficient to identify the content and outcome of the updater connections.
Review FILE-HD-01 SMB share-access and file-access auditing around 13:54:48 UTC to determine what the anonymous session accessed.
Check endpoint security detections and persistence or execution evidence for the updater and any files it created.
